# Appeal of Denial — Partial Knee Replacement (CPT 27446)

**RE: Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-01**
**Member: Reese Mercado | Member ID: W529317483**
**Reference Number: POC-8AD74FF769-66861**
**Governing Policy: Cigna CMM-311 Knee Replacement/Arthroplasty V1.0.2026 (Partial Knee Replacement section), effective 2026-08-04**
**Policy source: https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-311%20Knee%20Replac%20Arthro_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.20.2026.pdf**

Dear Cigna Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my request for a partial knee replacement (CPT 27446). My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I believe the records already in my file support that conclusion under Cigna's own coverage criteria.

## Why I believe this denial should be reconsidered

The denial notice states that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." My MRI from 2026-06-08 shows full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment of my knee, with bone-on-bone contact and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 changes limited to that compartment. This is the kind of single-compartment, severe structural finding that a partial (unicompartmental) knee replacement is designed to address.

Cigna's own policy states that:

> "unicompartmental replacement is considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria have been met:"

The policy then lists these specific requirements:

> "◦ function-limiting pain at short distances (e.g., walking less than one-quarter mile, limiting activity to two [2] city blocks, the equivalent to walking the length of a shopping mall) ◦ loss of knee function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment • Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months' duration ◦ Criteria exception:"

Here is how my records match up against each part of that standard:

- **Function-limiting pain / loss of function affecting daily activities:** My chart documents that I cannot climb stairs without assistance and that I wake 3–4 times nightly because of knee pain. This is a functional limitation that interferes with ordinary daily activities. [If a specific walking-distance limitation was also documented by Dr. Lindqvist's office, that detail should be added here to directly match the policy's example of function-limiting pain at short distances.]

- **Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months:** My records show NSAIDs used for 8 months with inadequate relief, a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-18 that gave only 3 weeks of partial relief, and 8 weeks of supervised physical therapy (24 visits, 2026-05-12 to 2026-07-07). Taken together, this non-surgical management spans well beyond the three-month period the policy requires, and it did not resolve my symptoms.

The policy also provides that:

> "Provider-directed non-surgical management may be inappropriate."

and

> "The medical record must clearly document why provider-directed non-surgical management is not appropriate."

I am not relying on this exception, since I completed the conservative treatment described above; I mention it only to show that even under the stricter general rule, my treatment history meets the required duration and demonstrated failure.

Given that my MRI shows single-compartment, bone-on-bone disease, and my treatment history and functional limitations align with the plan's own listed criteria, I do not believe the stated reason for denial — that imaging does not support medical necessity — is consistent with the records already submitted.

## What I am asking for

I am requesting that Cigna reconsider this denial and approve the partial knee replacement (CPT 27446) based on the medical records and imaging already in my file, and any additional documentation my surgeon's office provides in support of this appeal.

## Deadline and how I am submitting this appeal

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-01-28. I am submitting it by logging into my.cigna.com to use the plan's appeal form, and/or by calling the number on my member ID card (1-800-244-6224), and I am also sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, as that address is specific to my plan.

Thank you for reconsidering my case.

Sincerely,

______________________________
Reese Mercado
Member ID: W529317483
Date: [date of signing]
Contact phone: [phone number]
Contact address: [mailing address]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
